holidays.name: National Chocolate Mint Day
holidays.description: A cool and creamy celebration of the classic pairing of chocolate and mint, from after-dinner mints to mint chocolate chip ice cream and Thin Mint-style cookies.
holidays.origin: Like many food observances, it comes from the American tradition of unofficial national food days, popularized by food brands, bloggers, and social media. There is no single known founder.
holidays.funFact: Mint chocolate chip is consistently one of America's most popular ice cream flavors, and people tend to either love it or insist toothpaste should never be dessert.

holidays.name: National Lash Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating eyelashes, mascara, lash extensions, and all things fluttery. Participants are encouraged to bat their lashes with confidence.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial beauty observance, mostly promoted by the cosmetics and beauty industries and by social media. Its exact origin is unclear.
holidays.funFact: Eyelashes typically last about 6 to 10 weeks before falling out and growing back, and they exist to protect your eyes from dust and debris.

holidays.name: Copernicus Day (Nicolaus Copernicus's Birthday)
holidays.description: A celebration of the astronomer who proposed that the Sun, not the Earth, sits at the center of the universe, a notion that rearranged the cosmos and annoyed a lot of people.
holidays.origin: Copernicus was born on February 19, 1473, in Toruń, Poland. His heliocentric model was published in 1543 in 'On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres.'
holidays.funFact: Copernicus was also a physician, economist, and diplomat, and he reportedly saw a printed copy of his famous book only around the day he died.

holidays.name: Armed Forces Day (Lesser-Known Observances: Day of Remembrance Adjacent) / Family Time Pillow Fight Moment
holidays.description: A day for gathering the household for the sort of cushion combat that leaves everyone laughing and feathers on the ceiling fan.
holidays.origin: This is an informal, playful observance with no official founder, spread through family and parenting circles as a reminder to goof off together.
holidays.funFact: Organized pillow fight events happen worldwide, and the International Pillow Fight Day tradition draws crowds who are asked to use soft pillows and avoid hitting people who do not want to participate.
